sections.label: The opening
sections.line: Five articles and three vaults on insuring agents
sections.para: One question, who could underwrite an agent behaviour policy, answered in four articles: the definition, the market, the vendor's share, and where to build it. This one ties them together and shows the three vaults where the ideas run, with the same row of cards on every article.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Eight lines: the question, four answers, vaults, thread
sections.para: The definition prices each row; the market starts with a managing agent; the vendor carries a share of its rows; London underwrites and carries the risk and the money buys cover; three vaults run it; capped rows make it arithmetic; every article carries the series.

sections.label: The question
sections.line: One question, answered in order across the series
sections.para: If RiskMandate writes behaviour policies, who could underwrite them, and what would that look like? The series answered what would be insured first, then who could carry it, who should share it, and where and with how much.

sections.label: 1. A payout for every row
sections.line: Each named row has a limit and a price
sections.para: A behaviour policy's grant, mandate and delta read as an insurance policy: a limit per row, a lower premium per enforced control, nothing for unnamed rows. Uncontrolled: £69,850 for £80,000 of cover; with five enforced controls on a certified runtime, £6,720.

sections.label: 2. Who carries the risk
sections.line: Five companies sell agent cover; none per row
sections.para: AIUC, Armilla, Testudo, Munich Re and Harbor sell or distribute AI agent cover, none priced per row. The industry separates measuring, pricing, the balance sheet and reinsurance, so a new company starts as a managing agent, as Coalition and At-Bay did.

sections.label: 3. The vendor's layer
sections.line: The vendor carries a share of its product's rows
sections.para: The model's answer is the vendor's product, the access granted the customer's. Vendors' terms cap at a year's fees; Microsoft's guardrail-conditional cover shows the shape. In the worked example, the vendor carries £1,816 of £6,720.

sections.label: 4. Where to build the agent insurer
sections.line: London to underwrite and carry; money buys cover
sections.para: Start in London as a managing agent and coverholder and carry the risk there; sell into the US and EU; raise from investors. About £4.35 million runs it for two years; £10 million backs £94 to £188 million of cover, £50 million up to £1.52 billion.

sections.label: The vaults, where it runs
sections.line: Three vaults where the ideas run
sections.para: Licence to Operate simulates a policy priced reply by reply; the agent underwriting calculator holds the series' formula; AIUC-1 as a graph asks what would be insurable. Each opens read-only with its published read key.

sections.label: One thread through all of it
sections.line: Capped rows can be priced, split and capitalised
sections.para: A behaviour policy names rows; named rows can be capped, priced by a checkable formula, split with the vendor, and backed by capital bounded from the limits sold. None of it is built as insurance yet; the next step is insurers, vendors and investors.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: A summary of proposals, with illustrative numbers
sections.para: The detail and sources are in the four articles; the numbers are illustrative; nobody has agreed to any of it; the vault screenshots are of 28 October 2026; AIUC-1 as a graph is unofficial.

sections.line: The four articles, and screenshots of the vaults
sections.para: Written at Dinis's request after the four articles; the vault screenshots were taken in a headless browser on 28 October 2026 with each published read key; the series collage uses the articles' own lead figures.
